name: Alabama
trivia: Home to the world's first electric trolley system.
The University of Alabama's Crimson Tide football program has captured 18 recognized national championships.

name: Alaska
trivia: Has a longer coastline than all other U.S. states combined.
The University of Alaska Fairbanks runs one of the world's most active auroral research programs and even operates its own rocket range.

name: Arizona
trivia: Does not observe Daylight Saving Time.
Arizona State University in Tempe is the largest public university in the U.S. by on-campus enrollment, with over 145,000 students.

name: Arkansas
trivia: Contains the only active diamond mine in the United States.
The University of Arkansas houses the Clinton School of Public Service — the only school in the U.S. offering a Master of Public Service degree.

name: California
trivia: If California were a country, it would have the 5th largest economy in the world.
Stanford University alumni have founded companies whose combined revenue would rank as one of the world's largest economies.

name: Colorado
trivia: Has the highest mean elevation of any U.S. state.
The University of Colorado Boulder is home to five Nobel laureates and one of the largest university-based space research programs in the world.

name: Connecticut
trivia: Home to the first hamburger, served at Louis' Lunch in New Haven.
Yale University, founded in 1701, is the third-oldest institution of higher education in the U.S. and holds one of the world's largest academic libraries.

name: Delaware
trivia: The first state to ratify the U.S. Constitution.
The University of Delaware, chartered in 1743, counts three signers of the Declaration of Independence among its earliest students.

name: Florida
trivia: Produces more than 70% of the nation's oranges.
Gatorade was invented at the University of Florida in 1965 to keep the Gators football team hydrated in the Florida heat.

name: Georgia
trivia: Produces more peanuts and pecans than any other US state.
Georgia Tech's engineering program is consistently ranked among the top ten in the world — former President Jimmy Carter is one of its most famous alumni.

name: Hawaii
trivia: The state alphabet has only 12 letters.
The University of Hawaii at Mānoa runs one of only a handful of U.S. astronomy programs with observatories atop Mauna Kea, among the world's premier sky-viewing sites.

name: Idaho
trivia: Produces nearly one-third of the potatoes grown in the U.S.
The University of Idaho was the first land-grant university in the Pacific Northwest, chartered in 1889 — a year before Idaho became a state.

name: Illinois
trivia: First state to ratify the 13th Amendment abolishing slavery.
The University of Chicago has produced 100 Nobel laureates — more per capita than any other university in the world.

name: Indiana
trivia: The Indianapolis 500 is the largest single-day sporting event in the world.
Notre Dame's iconic Golden Dome atop the main building is coated in real 23-karat gold leaf, replaced roughly every 15 to 20 years.

name: Iowa
trivia: Pigs outnumber people by more than 7 to 1 in this state.
The Iowa Writers' Workshop at the University of Iowa was the first creative-writing MFA program in the world and has produced 17 Pulitzer Prize winners.

name: Kansas
trivia: Produces enough wheat in a year to bake 36 billion loaves of bread.
The first basketball coach at the University of Kansas was James Naismith — the man who invented the game.

name: Kentucky
trivia: Produces 95% of the world's bourbon.
The University of Kentucky men's basketball program holds the most wins in NCAA Division I history.

name: Louisiana
trivia: The only state that does not have counties; it has parishes instead.
Tulane University's medical school was the first in the Deep South, founded in 1834 to combat yellow-fever outbreaks in New Orleans.

name: Maine
trivia: The only U.S. state whose name has exactly one syllable.
Bowdoin College in Brunswick counts Nathaniel Hawthorne, Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, and President Franklin Pierce among its 19th-century alumni.

name: Maryland
trivia: Donated the land that became Washington, D.C.
The U.S. Naval Academy in Annapolis has commissioned every officer graduating since 1845 directly into the Navy or Marine Corps.

name: Massachusetts
trivia: Invented both basketball and volleyball.
Harvard University, founded in 1636, is the oldest institution of higher learning in the United States and holds the world's largest academic library.

name: Michigan
trivia: You are never more than 6 miles from a body of water in this state.
The University of Michigan's Big House is the largest college football stadium in America, seating over 107,000 fans.

name: Minnesota
trivia: Has an actual tally of 11,842 lakes, despite its nickname.
University of Minnesota researchers invented the retractable seat belt, the implantable cardiac pacemaker, and the flight data recorder.

name: Mississippi
trivia: The teddy bear was named after a hunting trip in this state by Theodore Roosevelt.
The University of Mississippi (Ole Miss) is home to the National Center for Physical Acoustics, one of the world's leading acoustics research centers.

name: Missouri
trivia: Eight different states border this one, tied for the most with Tennessee.
Washington University in St. Louis has produced 25 Nobel laureates and is consistently ranked among the top medical schools in the U.S.

name: Montana
trivia: Contains the largest migratory elk herd in the nation.
The University of Montana in Missoula opened one of the earliest Schools of Forestry in the American West, admitting its first students in 1913.

name: Nebraska
trivia: Home to the world's largest indoor rainforest.
The University of Nebraska–Lincoln football program set the longest home-sellout streak in college football history — 375 consecutive games.

name: Nevada
trivia: The driest state in the U.S., averaging only 7 inches of rain per year.
UNLV's Harrah College of Hospitality is consistently ranked the top hospitality school in the world.

name: New Hampshire
trivia: Hosts the first primary in the U.S. presidential election cycle.
Dartmouth College is the smallest school in the Ivy League and the ninth-oldest college in the U.S., founded in 1769 by a charter from King George III.

name: New Jersey
trivia: Has the highest population density of any U.S. state.
Princeton University's Firestone Library is the largest open-stack academic library in the world, holding more than 13 million volumes.

name: New Mexico
trivia: Santa Fe is the highest elevation capital city in the U.S.
Los Alamos National Laboratory, born from the Manhattan Project, remains one of the world's largest multidisciplinary research institutions.

name: New York
trivia: The first capital of the United States was New York City.
Columbia University administers the Pulitzer Prize each year and counts more than 100 Nobel laureates among its alumni and faculty.

name: North Carolina
trivia: Grows the most sweet potatoes of any state.
The Research Triangle links Duke, UNC-Chapel Hill, and NC State — the largest research park in the U.S. by land area.

name: North Dakota
trivia: Grows more sunflowers than any other state.
The University of North Dakota was the first American university to offer a fully accredited four-year aviation degree program.

name: Ohio
trivia: Known as the 'Mother of Presidents', having produced seven U.S. Presidents.
Ohio State University enrolls over 60,000 undergraduates and its marching band is the largest all-brass band in the world.

name: Oklahoma
trivia: Has more man-made lakes than any other state.
The University of Oklahoma's Sam Noble Museum houses the largest Apatosaurus skeleton ever mounted for public display.

name: Oregon
trivia: Home to Crater Lake, the deepest lake in the United States.
The University of Oregon is where Nike founder Phil Knight and coach Bill Bowerman first tested the running shoes that grew into the Nike brand.

name: Pennsylvania
trivia: The first daily newspaper in the U.S. was published in Philadelphia.
The University of Pennsylvania was founded by Benjamin Franklin in 1740 and is home to the Wharton School — the world's first collegiate business school.

name: Rhode Island
trivia: The smallest state in size, but shares a state water border with New York.
Brown University's Open Curriculum lets undergraduates choose any courses they want with no core requirements — unique among the Ivies.

name: South Carolina
trivia: The first state to secede from the Union during the Civil War.
Clemson University was founded on land bequeathed by Thomas Green Clemson, son-in-law of Vice President John C. Calhoun.

name: South Dakota
trivia: Home to the largest and most complete T-Rex skeleton ever found.
The South Dakota School of Mines & Technology reports the highest starting-salary rate for graduates of any public university in the U.S.

name: Tennessee
trivia: Tied with Missouri for bordering the most states (eight).
Vanderbilt University was founded with a $1 million gift from railroad magnate Cornelius Vanderbilt — the only philanthropic donation of his lifetime.

name: Texas
trivia: Was an independent nation from 1836 to 1845.
The University of Texas at Austin has one of the ten largest university endowments in the world and one of the largest single-campus enrollments in the country.

name: Utah
trivia: The Great Salt Lake is saltier than the ocean.
Brigham Young University offers instruction in more than 60 languages — the most of any undergraduate university in the U.S.

name: Vermont
trivia: The largest producer of maple syrup in the U.S.
Middlebury College's Language Schools are so intensive that students take an oath to speak only their studied language for the entire summer.

name: Virginia
trivia: Home to the first permanent English settlement in the Americas (Jamestown).
The University of Virginia was founded and designed by Thomas Jefferson in 1819 — he considered it one of his three greatest life achievements.

name: Washington
trivia: The only state named after a U.S. President.
The University of Washington runs one of the largest medical research operations of any public university in the world.

name: West Virginia
trivia: The first state to have a sales tax.
West Virginia University in Morgantown operates the world's longest fully automated Personal Rapid Transit system, connecting three of its campuses.

name: Wisconsin
trivia: Produces more cheese than any other state in the U.S.
Vitamins A and B were both isolated by researchers at the University of Wisconsin–Madison in the early 20th century.

name: Wyoming
trivia: The first state to grant women the right to vote.
The University of Wyoming is the only four-year public university in the state and guarantees scholarship consideration to every Wyoming high-school graduate.

name: Alberta
trivia: Named after Princess Louise Caroline Alberta, fourth daughter of Queen Victoria.
The University of Alberta in Edmonton is one of Canada's top research universities and has produced Nobel laureates and Rhodes Scholars.

name: British Columbia
trivia: Produces over half of all Canadian wine.
The University of British Columbia sits on a 1,000-acre oceanfront campus in Vancouver and consistently ranks among the top 40 universities in the world.

name: Manitoba
trivia: Churchill, Manitoba is known as the polar bear capital of the world.
The University of Manitoba, founded in 1877, was the first university established in Western Canada.

name: New Brunswick
trivia: The only officially bilingual province in Canada (English and French).
The University of New Brunswick, founded in 1785, is the oldest English-language university in Canada and the third-oldest in North America.

name: Newfoundland and Labrador
trivia: Has its own unique timezone, off by 30 minutes.
Memorial University in St. John's was founded to memorialize Newfoundlanders killed in the World Wars and remains Atlantic Canada's largest university.

name: Nova Scotia
trivia: Produces more lobster than any other province in Canada.
Dalhousie University in Halifax is home to one of the world's leading ocean research programs, powered by its Atlantic-coast location.

name: Northwest Territories
trivia: Known as the Diamond Capital of North America.
The Aurora Research Institute in Inuvik has studied the aurora borealis and Arctic permafrost for more than 50 years.

name: Nunavut
trivia: The largest, newest, and least populous territory of Canada.
Nunavut Arctic College is the territory's only post-secondary institution and delivers programs in both English and Inuktitut.

name: Ontario
trivia: Contains more than 250,000 lakes.
Insulin was discovered at the University of Toronto in 1921 — a breakthrough that earned the university a Nobel Prize the following year.

name: Prince Edward Island
trivia: The smallest province in both area and population.
The University of Prince Edward Island is home to the Atlantic Veterinary College — one of only five veterinary schools in all of Canada.

name: Quebec
trivia: Produces more than 70% of the world's maple syrup.
McGill University, founded in 1821 by fur trader James McGill, is consistently ranked among the top universities in the world.

name: Saskatchewan
trivia: The only province with completely artificial boundaries.
The University of Saskatchewan led the development of canola oil in the 1970s — one of Canada's most successful agricultural innovations.

name: Yukon
trivia: Home to Canada's highest peak, Mount Logan.
Yukon University became Canada's first university north of 60° in 2020, with programs deeply shaped by the territory's Indigenous cultures.
